newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gov't plans no more June coffee stock sales.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gov't plans no more June coffee stock sales.

text.p: Brazil's government is not planning any additional auctions of government coffee stocks in June unless a shock such as a frost drives prices sharply higher, top government commodity officials said.

The next official auction has been set for July 2 although the quantity has not yet been decided, Jose Monteiro, head of the National Coffee Department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry, told reporters at a coffee fair in Sao Paulo.
"An auction between now (and July 2) would be difficult but what we can do is increase the quantity a little," said Mauricio Assis, head of the ministry's primary commodities department.

An auction today of 42,250 60-kg bags was a complete sell-out while almost all of the 150,000 bags offered in a sale last week were sold at closing prices generally well above opening levels set by the government.
Domestic roasters citing tight market supply are demanding that an additional 200,000 bags be put up for sale this month.
"Of course if there is a frost or some other event that pushes the market higher, the government could eventually hold an intermediary auction," Monteiro said.
Government stocks currently stand at 12.9 million bags, Assis said.

Brazil's domestic soluble industry has also been complaining to the government about high domestic prices which it claims is affecting Brazilian companies' competitiveness given other soluble producers can buy raw materials more cheaply.

Already one key producer has considered importing roasted coffee for processing from India but the government is now studying a plan to lend part of its coffee stocks to the soluble industry in order to avert imports, Monteiro said.
"The government is studying a solution for the soluble industry...including a proposal to lend its stocks," he said.

The government would also benefit as it could clear out old stock and receive new crop coffee at a later date from the soluble industry at warehouses specified by the government, making its warehousing network more efficient, Monteiro said.
